theory: The claim that every data change changes the mean contradicts adding a value equal to the mean. Removing a smallest or largest value changes the mean strictly only when that value is below or above the mean and values remain. Removing an extreme need not change the range when another copy remains. Qualify the claims that an outlier always moves the median only slightly or makes the range much bigger, and that larger datasets always reduce an extra value's effect: the latter comparison requires the same original mean and added value.
